C2: The driver's reply one minute later, 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4), is a threat to deprive the rider of her means of exit, spoken by the person who controls the door locks; on its face it is intimidation within SAFE-1 and must go to a human reviewer rather than be auto-adjudicated. [F4] [SAFE-1]
C3: The chat record is complete (2 messages, every one timestamped, F5), so the threat in F4 is not a fragment of an incomplete or unverifiable exchange — the record itself establishes what was said and when. [F5] [SAFE-1]
C4: The driver's own written statement confirms he refused to let the rider out and drove on: 'The rider tried to open the door at the lights. I told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on' (F6) — so the refusal to stop is admitted, and his safety rationale is a claim, not rider consent to stay in the car. [F6] [SAFE-1 RD-5]
C5: The record rules out any route-deviation explanation for the rider's distress: actual distance 15.4 km versus optimal 15.5 km, -0.1 km / -0% (F1), and duration 23.7 min versus 21.8 min (F2) — the ride went the direct way, so the incident was about the rider being kept in the car, not about the route. [F1 F2] [RD-1]

[F7 F8] [SAFE-1]

F4 is not supported beyond the chat record (F5); there is no GPS evidence of the car being stopped at traffic lights while the rider tried to open the door, so that detail in F6 is the driver's word alone.

events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The dispute is filed as a safety incident and the anonymised trace marks it SAFE-1 with the only permitted outcome escalate, so I do not adjudicate any element of it and instead hand a factual summary to a human reviewer [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

What happened, per the record: at 17:09 the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; one minute later, at 17:10, the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. The chat record contains exactly these two messages and every one is timestamped [F5], so the exchange is complete and nothing earlier or later is missing. The driver's written statement after the trip says the rider tried to open the door at the lights and that he told her to sit down "for her own safety" and drove on [F6]. So the driver does not deny speaking the words in [F4]; what is disputed is how those words are to be read — a safety instruction in a moving car or an intimidation of a rider who had asked to leave — and that reading is reserved to the human reviewer, not to this tribunal, under SAFE-1 [F3][F4][F6].

This is not a routing case and no money turns on it. The actual distance was 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route, i.e. 0.1 km shorter [F1], and the trip took 23.7 min against a 21.8 min estimate [F2]; no off-route segment and no fare fact appear in the file, and the trip is a fixed-fare RydeX trip, so RD-1 and RD-2 supply no refundable amount and I compute none [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2]. The rider's advocate withdrew any fare claim for the same reason [F1][F2].

The profiles are neutral and decide nothing: the rider has 619 days, a 4.8 rating and no disputes in 90 days [F7], and the driver has 893 days, a 4.62 rating, 1038 trips in 90 days and no disputes or upheld complaints [F8]. With no upheld prior matter against the driver, the RD-6 precondition is absent, so I attach no flag_account to this recommendation [F8][RD-6]; both advocates also asked for no such action [F7][F8].

Safety screen (read in full): the case is itself a safety complaint — the rider says the driver "threatened to lock me in" and felt unsafe for the whole ride, and the driver's recorded words are "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4], following her request to be let out [F3]. Read in context [F4] is a statement about controlling the doors of the car by the person who controls them, aimed at a rider who had just asked to exit, so I record it as a suspected safety concern (intimidation / deprivation of means of exit) and escalate it rather than rule; the driver's "for her own safety" motive [F6] is his own untimestamped statement and cannot be weighed here [F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1]. I find no allegation of collision, injury or dangerous driving, so SAFE-2 is not engaged on this record [F6][SAFE-2]. Because safety_concern is suspected, no ruling is issued and the outcome is escalate [SAFE-1].

Evidence status: sufficient for the disposition I reach. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F5], and it contains the two utterances on which the escalation rests [F3][F4]; the fare is a fixed quote that needs no computation and the GPS facts settle that there was no route deviation [F1][F2]. I therefore name no evidence gap.

Matters for the reviewer to test: whether the driver's account in [F6] that the rider "tried to open the door at the lights" is supported by anything other than his own statement (the file carries no telematics, camera or GPS evidence of a door attempt or of the car being stopped) [F6]; whether the driver continued the ride after a clear request to be let out [F3][F4][F6]; and whether either party's conduct engages Ryde's code of conduct beyond this incident [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. actions.detail: Filled as a safety incident; the completed chat shows a rider request to be let out at 17:09 [F3] followed at 17:10 by the driver's "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4], and his statement admits he told her to sit down and drove on [F6]. claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out mid-trip: at 17:09 she wrote 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here' (F3). A passenger's request to end the ride and leave the car is a routing/destination instruction the driver must respect under RD-3(a).

The driver's reply one minute later, 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4), is a threat to deprive the rider of her means of exit, spoken by the person who controls the door locks; on its face it is intimidation within SAFE-1 and must go to a human reviewer rather than be auto-adjudicated.

The chat record is complete (2 messages, every one timestamped, F5), so the threat in F4 is not a fragment of an incomplete or unverifiable exchange — the record itself establishes what was said and when.

The driver's own written statement confirms he refused to let the rider out and drove on: 'The rider tried to open the door at the lights. I told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on' (F6) — so the refusal to stop is admitted, and his safety rationale is a claim, not rider consent to stay in the car.

The record rules out any route-deviation explanation for the rider's distress: actual distance 15.4 km versus optimal 15.5 km, -0.1 km / -0% (F1), and duration 23.7 min versus 21.8 min (F2) — the ride went the direct way, so the incident was about the rider being kept in the car, not about the route.

The rider has 619 days of account history, a 4.8 rating and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days (F7), so her safety complaint is not the product of a pattern of unsupported claims; the driver's clean dispute history (F8) does not neutralise an admitted threat recorded in the chat.

weaknesses: The complaint's framing ('threatened to lock me in') rests on a single chat line; the driver's statement (F6) puts a safety motive on it ('for her own safety'), and a judge may read F4 as a safety instruction rather than a threat. There is no allegation of physical contact, injury or dangerous driving, so SAFE-2 is not clearly engaged.

No fare or GPS fact shows any money loss tied to the incident: there is no off-route segment (F1 shows -0.1 km, F2 a 23.7 min trip), the fare is a fixed RydeX quote with no fare facts returned, and traffic facts are absent — so any refund request is unsupported and the only available outcome is escalation, not compensation. F4 is not supported beyond the chat record (F5); there is no GPS evidence of the car being stopped at traffic lights while the rider tried to open the door, so that detail in F6 is the driver's word alone.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is a safety allegation — she says the driver 'threatened to lock me in' — and the only record of any words spoken or written is the driver's message at 17:10: 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' (F4), which the rider herself reports as her account of feeling unsafe (F3, F4). A safety allegation of this kind is not something this tribunal resolves on the papers; it must go to a person.

The chat record is complete: two messages, every one timestamped (F5), so no part of the exchange is missing; the record contains one rider request at 17:09 to stop (F3) and one driver reply at 17:10 (F4), and nothing else was said.

The driver's written statement (F6) says he told the rider to sit down 'for her own safety' and drove on after she tried to open the door at the lights; read against the 17:09 rider message (F3) this is an account of refusing to let a rider step out of a moving vehicle into traffic, not of detaining her — a reading a human reviewer, not this tribunal, should test.

There is no route-deviation or overcharge element in the complaint: the GPS records the actual distance as 15.4 km against an optimal route of 15.5 km, i.e. 0.1 km shorter (F1), and this is a fixed-fare RydeX trip, so the $32.86 charge is unaffected by any deviation.

The trip was completed in 23.7 minutes against a 21.8-minute estimate, only 1.9 minutes over (F2), which is inconsistent with an alleged prolonged confinement in the car; the rider was delivered to Bedok Mall (F2).

The driver has 893 days on the platform, a 4.62 rating, 1038 trips in 90 days and zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in that window (F8); the rider has 619 days, a 4.8 rating and zero disputes in 90 days (F7). The histories give no basis for a flag_account action against the driver.

weaknesses: The rider's own words in the complaint — 'threatened to lock me in' — and the driver's recorded words 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' (F4) read plainly as an intimidation allegation; the driver's statement (F6) does not deny saying it, and whether 'for her own safety' excuses the phrasing is exactly the judgement this tribunal cannot make. The rider's 17:09 request to be let out (F3) shows she felt she could not leave.

The 200 m / route corridor data does not cover the allegation at all: F1 only shows distance is 0.1 km shorter, so nothing in the system records clears the driver of the safety allegation on its merits, even though it does clear him on route and fare.
The rider profile (F7) is unblemished — 619 days, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days — so there is no history to argue she is a vexatious complainant.

The driver's account that the rider 'tried to open the door' (F6) is a statement with no GPS or other record behind it; per the record rules, a statement alone cannot outweigh the rider's account, and there is no camera or telematics fact to support the driver's version of the incident (F3, F4).

points.response: Conceded on the outcome: the rider's safety allegation and the driver's recorded words 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4), read against her 17:09 request to be let out (F3), are an intimidation allegation that belongs to a human reviewer under SAFE-1, so I join the driver in asking for escalate — I do not ask this tribunal to find the threat proven.

Agreed that the record is complete (F5), which is precisely why it can be read without speculation: the exchange consists of one rider request at 17:09 (F3) and one driver reply at 17:10 (F4), and nothing in that complete record shows the rider withdrawing her request to get out or consenting to stay in the car (F3, F4, F5).

The driver's 'for her own safety' motive is his own written statement (F6) and, like the 'tried to open the door at the lights' detail in the same sentence, has no GPS, camera or telematics record behind it, so on the record rules it cannot outweigh the rider's contemporaneous account in the completed chat (F3, F4, F5); the driver does not deny saying the words (F4), and it is the human reviewer who must test the motive.

No dispute there: the GPS shows actual 15.4 km against optimal 15.5 km, -0.1 km / -0% (F1), and no off-route segment or fare fact exists, so I make no route or fare claim and ask for no refund — the escalation rests entirely on the safety allegation (F3, F4).

The 23.7 min versus 21.8 min comparison (F2) says nothing about the confinement allegation: the rider's request to be let out at 17:09 (F3) was followed by the driver refusing and driving on (F4, F6), and completion of the trip at Bedok Mall does not answer whether she was kept in the car after asking to leave.

I ask for no flag_account against the driver: his 893 days, 4.62 rating and zero upheld complaints (F8) give no RD-6 basis, but that same clean-history argument (F7, F8) equally removes any suggestion that the rider's safety report is a vexatious claim, leaving the completed chat (F3, F4, F5) as the neutral thing for the reviewer to read.

Conceded in part: the rider did ask to get out (F3), but RD-3 governs stops and route changes ordered by the rider, and the record here (F3) is a request, not an agreed stop — the driver's 17:10 answer (F4) is a refusal, and nothing in the record shows the car stopped or the route changed anywhere. RD-3 therefore decides nothing about this safety complaint, which is why the case belongs with a human under SAFE-1 (F4, F5).

Not contested as to escalation: I ask for the same outcome. On the merits, whether F4 is a threat or an instruction to stay seated in a moving car is a semantic judgement this tribunal does not make — SAFE-1 itself says a human reads the words — so the correct disposition is escalate (F4, F5).

Agreed: the chat is complete and fully timestamped (F5), which is a point in my favour too — there is no missing message before or after F4 in which the rider asked again, or in which anything further was said (F3, F4).

The rider's own F6 reading is right that the driver's statement admits he told her to sit down and drove on (F6); but F6 is the driver's word alone and cuts both ways: it says the door was opened at the lights because the car was stopped in traffic, which is why he told her to sit down before the lights turned rather than let her step into moving traffic — a version only a human reviewer, not this tribunal, can weigh against the rider's account (F3, F4).

I rely on the same record: the car travelled 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route (F1) and completed in 23.7 min against 21.8 min (F2), so the ride was the direct way and delivered the rider to Bedok Mall — this is one of only two facts in the file that is independent of both parties' words, and it shows no deviation, no detour and no prolonged confinement on the road (F1, F2).

The disputed history does not help either side, so the complaint must stand on F4 alone: the rider's clean 90 days (F7) and the driver's 1038 trips with zero disputes and zero upheld (F8) are profile facts that may never decide the case, and on F8 there is no basis for any flag_account action against the driver (F8).

Restated for completeness, not withdrawn: this is a fixed-fare RydeX trip and the GPS shows the actual distance 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route (F1), so no refund of any fare item is computable from any fare or GPS fact and neither side can ask for compensation here.
